시편-42-1.title: 시편 42장 1절 역사문법적 주해
시편-42-1.exegesis: 11-13. favourest-- or tenderly lovest me ( Ge 34:19 ), evinced by relief from his enemies, and, farther, God recognizes his innocence by upholding him.
시편-42-1.theologicalNote: 11-13. favourest-- or tenderly lovest me ( Ge 34:19 ), evinced by relief from his enemies, and, farther, God recognizes his innocence by upholding him.

시편-42-2.title: 시편 42장 2절 역사문법적 주해
시편-42-2.exegesis: PSALM 42 Psa 42:1-11 . Maschil--(See on Psa 32:1 , title). For, or of (see Introduction) the sons of Korah. The writer, perhaps one of this Levitical family of singers accompanying David in exile, mourns his absence from the sanctuary, a cause of grief aggravated by the taunts of enemies, and is comforted in hopes of relief. This course of thought is repeated with some variety of detail, but closing with the same refrain. 1-2. Compare ( Psa 63:1 ). panteth-- desires in a state of exhaustion.

시편-42-4.title: 시편 42장 4절 역사문법적 주해
시편-42-4.exegesis: 3. Where is thy God?-- implying that He had forsaken him (compare 2Sa 16:7 ; Psa 3:2 ; 22:8 ).
시편-42-4.theologicalNote: 3. Where is thy God?-- implying that He had forsaken him (compare 2Sa 16:7 ; Psa 3:2 ; 22:8 ).

시편-42-5.title: 시편 42장 5절 역사문법적 주해
시편-42-5.exegesis: 4. The verbs are properly rendered as futures, "I will remember," &c.,-- that is, the recollection of this season of distress will give greater zest to the privileges of God's worship, when obtained.
시편-42-5.theologicalNote: 4. The verbs are properly rendered as futures, "I will remember," &c.,-- that is, the recollection of this season of distress will give greater zest to the privileges of God's worship, when obtained.

시편-42-6.title: 시편 42장 6절 역사문법적 주해
시편-42-6.exegesis: 5. Hence he chides his despondent soul, assuring himself of a time of joy. help of his countenance-- or, "face" (compare Nu 6:25 ; Psa 4:6 ; 16:11 ).
시편-42-6.theologicalNote: 5. Hence he chides his despondent soul, assuring himself of a time of joy. help of his countenance-- or, "face" (compare Nu 6:25 ; Psa 4:6 ; 16:11 ).

시편-42-7.title: 시편 42장 7절 역사문법적 주해
시편-42-7.exegesis: 6. Dejection again described. therefore-- that is, finding no comfort in myself, I turn to Thee, even in this distant "land of Jordan and the (mountains) Hermon, the country east of Jordan. hill Mizar-- as a name of a small hill contrasted with the mountains round about Jerusalem, perhaps denoted the contempt with which the place of exile was regarded.

시편-42-8.title: 시편 42장 8절 역사문법적 주해
시편-42-8.exegesis: 7. The roar of successive billows, responding to that of floods of rain, represented the heavy waves of sorrow which overwhelmed him.
시편-42-8.theologicalNote: 7. The roar of successive billows, responding to that of floods of rain, represented the heavy waves of sorrow which overwhelmed him.

시편-42-9.title: 시편 42장 9절 역사문법적 주해
시편-42-9.exegesis: 8. Still he relies on as constant a flow of divine mercy which will elicit his praise and encourage his prayer to God.
시편-42-9.theologicalNote: 8. Still he relies on as constant a flow of divine mercy which will elicit his praise and encourage his prayer to God.

시편-42-10.title: 시편 42장 10절 역사문법적 주해
시편-42-10.exegesis: 9-10. in view of which [Psa 42:8], he dictates to himself a prayer based on his distress, aggravated as it was by the cruel taunts and infidel suggestions of his foes.
시편-42-10.theologicalNote: 9-10. in view of which [Psa 42:8], he dictates to himself a prayer based on his distress, aggravated as it was by the cruel taunts and infidel suggestions of his foes.
